ramayana-2-65-19.meaning: The city has lost its joy.
ramayana-2-65-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-20.translation: Leading men are not seen going out or coming in on carriages, elephants or horses as before.
ramayana-2-65-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-21.translation: I see many kinds of unwelcome, evil and unpleasant omens; that is why my mind sinks.
ramayana-2-65-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-22.translation: With his horses tired he entered by the Vaijayanta gate. The gatekeepers rose, wished him victory, and went with him.
ramayana-2-65-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-23.translation: His mind unsettled, Raghava returned the greeting of the gatekeepers and spoke there to Ashvapati's weary charioteer.
ramayana-2-65-23.meaning: He is troubled as he speaks.
ramayana-2-65-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-24.translation: Charioteer, all the signs we have heard of before that come at the death of kings, I see here.
ramayana-2-65-24.meaning: He recognises signs of a king's death.
ramayana-2-65-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-25.translation: I see the people in the city, men and women, dirty, eyes full of tears, wretched, lost in thought, thin and anxious.
ramayana-2-65-25.meaning: The people show signs of mourning.
ramayana-2-65-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-26.translation: Having said this to the charioteer, Bharata, sad at heart, seeing these unwelcome signs in Ayodhya, went to the royal palace.
ramayana-2-65-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-27.translation: Seeing the city, once bright as Indra's city, its crossroads, houses and streets empty, its doors, panels and bolts reddened with dust, he was filled even more with sorrow.
ramayana-2-65-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-65-28.translation: Seeing many things unpleasant to the mind, which had never been in the city before, great-souled Bharata, head bowed, sad and joyless, entered his father's house.
ramayana-2-65-28.meaning: He enters his father's house with dread.
ramayana-2-65-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 65: Bharata's journey home over many rivers and forests takes seven nights. Approaching Ayodhya, he finds it silent and joyless and sees many bad omens. He enters his father's palace with a heavy heart.

ramayana-2-66-1.translation: Not seeing his father there in his father's residence, Bharata went to see his mother in his mother's residence.
ramayana-2-66-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-2.translation: Seeing her son, who had been away, arrive, Kaikeyi jumped up joyfully, leaving her golden seat.
ramayana-2-66-2.meaning: Kaikeyi is delighted to see him.
ramayana-2-66-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. ramayana-2-66-9.meaning: He hurried ahead of the caravan.
ramayana-2-66-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-10.translation: I have come hurried by messengers bringing the king's message. Mother, please tell me what I want to ask.
ramayana-2-66-10.meaning: Now he has questions of his own.
ramayana-2-66-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-11.translation: Your gold-adorned bed is empty, and these Ikshvaku people do not seem happy to me.
ramayana-2-66-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-12.translation: The king is usually here in mother's residence. I do not see him today, though I came here wanting to see him.
ramayana-2-66-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-13.translation: I will clasp my father's feet. Tell me, as I ask: or is he, mother, in the residence of the eldest, Kausalya?
ramayana-2-66-13.meaning: He wants to greet his father.
ramayana-2-66-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-14.translation: Kaikeyi, deluded by greed for the kingdom, knowing what he did not know, told him the terrible, unwelcome news as if it were pleasant: 'Your father has gone the way all beings go.'
ramayana-2-66-14.meaning: She announces his father's death coldly.
ramayana-2-66-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-15.translation: Hearing that, pure Bharata, of righteous birth, struck by the force of grief for his father, fell suddenly to the ground.
ramayana-2-66-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-16.translation: Then, wrapped in grief, pained by his father's death, the splendid one lamented, his mind confused and agitated.
ramayana-2-66-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-17.translation: This bed of my father used to look so beautiful before; today it does not shine, without that wise man.
ramayana-2-66-17.meaning: Everything reminds him of his father.
ramayana-2-66-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-18.translation: Seeing him, godlike and stricken, fallen on the ground, she lifted him up, grieving, and said this.
ramayana-2-66-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-19.translation: Get up, get up! Why do you lie there, famous prince? Good people like you, respected in assemblies, do not grieve.
ramayana-2-66-19.meaning: She tells him not to grieve.
ramayana-2-66-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-20.translation: After weeping a long time and rolling on the ground, covered by many sorrows, he replied to his mother.
ramayana-2-66-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-21.translation: I set out happily, thinking, 'The king will consecrate Rama, or will perform a sacrifice.'
ramayana-2-66-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-22.translation: But it has turned out otherwise, and my heart is broken, for I cannot see my father, who was always devoted to my welfare.
ramayana-2-66-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-23.translation: Mother, of what illness did the king die while I was away? Blessed are Rama and the others, who performed father's last rites themselves.
ramayana-2-66-23.meaning: He envies those who were there at the end.
ramayana-2-66-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-24.translation: Surely the famous great king does not know I have arrived, or my father would quickly bend down and kiss my head.
ramayana-2-66-24.meaning: He imagines his father's loving welcome.
ramayana-2-66-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-25.translation: Where is that pleasant-touching hand of my father, tireless in deeds, with which he used to wipe me clean when I was covered in dust?
ramayana-2-66-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-26.translation: Tell me quickly about Rama, tireless in deeds, who is my brother, father and kinsman, whose servant I am.
ramayana-2-66-26.meaning: He turns to Rama as his new father.
ramayana-2-66-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-27.translation: For a noble person who knows dharma, the eldest brother becomes a father. I will clasp his feet; he is now my refuge.
ramayana-2-66-27.meaning: Bharata sees Rama as head of the family.
ramayana-2-66-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-28.translation: Noble lady, what did the king, my father, true in valour, say? I want to hear his last good message for me.
ramayana-2-66-28.meaning: He asks for his father's last words.
ramayana-2-66-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-29.translation: Asked this, Kaikeyi told the truth: 'Lamenting "Rama! Alas Sita! Lakshmana!", that great soul, best of those who travel, went to the next world.'
ramayana-2-66-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-30.translation: This was your father's last speech, caught by the law of time like a great elephant by nooses:
ramayana-2-66-30.meaning: Death bound him like a snared elephant.
ramayana-2-66-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-31.translation: 'Fulfilled are the people who will see Rama come back with Sita, and mighty-armed Lakshmana returned.'
ramayana-2-66-31.meaning: His last wish was to see Rama again.
ramayana-2-66-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-32.translation: Hearing that second piece of unwelcome news, he was dejected, and with a downcast face he asked his mother again.
ramayana-2-66-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-33.translation: And where now is that righteous one, who increases Kausalya's joy, gone with his brother Lakshmana and with Sita?
ramayana-2-66-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-34.translation: Asked thus, his mother began to tell the truth, the unwelcome news, all at once, thinking it would please him.
ramayana-2-66-34.meaning: She thinks he will be glad.
ramayana-2-66-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-35.translation: Son, that prince has gone to the great Dandaka forest, wearing bark clothes, with Vaidehi, followed by Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-66-35.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-36.translation: Hearing that, Bharata was alarmed, fearing for his brother's conduct, and because of the greatness of his family began to ask.
ramayana-2-66-36.meaning: He fears Rama has done some wrong.
ramayana-2-66-36.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-37.translation: Has Rama perhaps taken some Brahmin's wealth? Has he harmed some innocent person, rich or poor?
ramayana-2-66-37.meaning: He asks what crime could cause exile.
ramayana-2-66-37.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-38.translation: Has the prince desired another man's wife? Why has he been exiled to the Dandaka forest like a murderer?
ramayana-2-66-38.meaning: He cannot imagine why Rama was banished.
ramayana-2-66-38.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-39.translation: Then his fickle mother began to describe her own deed exactly as it was, with that same nature.
ramayana-2-66-39.meaning: Kaikeyi tells him the truth plainly. The phrase 'woman's nature' is the narrator's dated judgment of Kaikeyi here, not a truth about women.
ramayana-2-66-39.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-40.translation: Rama took no Brahmin's wealth, harmed no innocent person rich or poor, and Rama does not even look at other men's wives.
ramayana-2-66-40.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-41.translation: But son, as soon as I heard of Rama's consecration, I asked your father for the kingdom for you and for Rama's exile.
ramayana-2-66-41.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-42.translation: Your father, keeping to his word, did just that, and Rama was sent away with Lakshmana and Sita.
ramayana-2-66-42.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-43.translation: Not seeing his beloved son, the famous king, worn out by grief for his son, died.
ramayana-2-66-43.meaning: The exile led to the king's death.
ramayana-2-66-43.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-44.translation: Now, knower of dharma, take up the kingship, for I have done all this for your sake.
ramayana-2-66-44.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-66-45.translation: So, son, quickly, with Vasishtha and the chief Brahmins who know the rites, perform the king's funeral and have yourself, of undaunted spirit, consecrated over the earth.
ramayana-2-66-45.meaning: She tells him to bury the king and take the throne.
ramayana-2-66-45.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 66: Not finding his father, Bharata goes to his mother Kaikeyi. She tells him plainly that Dasharatha is dead and that Rama has been exiled at her request, and urges him to take the throne. The narrator's remark about a woman's nature reflects the attitudes of the time and is aimed at Kaikeyi's actions here.

ramayana-2-67-1.translation: Hearing that his father had died and his two brothers had been exiled, Bharata, burning with sorrow, spoke these words.
ramayana-2-67-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-2.translation: What use is a kingdom to me, struck down and grieving, deprived of my father and of my brother who was like a father?
ramayana-2-67-2.meaning: The kingdom means nothing without his family.
ramayana-2-67-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-3.translation: You have added sorrow to my sorrow, like rubbing salt into a wound, by sending the king to his death and making Rama an ascetic.
ramayana-2-67-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-4.translation: You have come like the night of doom to destroy this family. My father embraced a burning coal and did not know it.
ramayana-2-67-4.meaning: He says his father trusted the one who would destroy him.
ramayana-2-67-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-5.translation: Kausalya and Sumitra, crushed by grief for their sons, will hardly be able to live now that they have you as my mother.
ramayana-2-67-5.meaning: He fears for the other queens.
ramayana-2-67-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-6.translation: Even the noble, righteous Rama, who knows how to treat elders, behaved towards you with the highest regard, as he would towards his own mother.
ramayana-2-67-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-7.translation: And my eldest mother, far-sighted Kausalya, following dharma, treated you like a sister.
ramayana-2-67-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-8.translation: Having sent her self-disciplined son into forest exile wearing bark clothes, how do you not grieve, wicked one?
ramayana-2-67-8.meaning: He cannot understand her lack of remorse.
ramayana-2-67-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata is horrified and denounces his mother for causing his father's death and Rama's exile.

ramayana-2-67-9.translation: Having banished the brave, glorious, self-disciplined hero, who sees no evil, in bark clothes, what reason do you see in it?
ramayana-2-67-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-10.translation: I think, greedy as you are, you did not know how I feel towards Raghava, and so for the sake of the kingdom you brought about this great disaster.
ramayana-2-67-10.meaning: She misjudged his loyalty to Rama.
ramayana-2-67-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-11.translation: Without seeing those two tigers among men, Rama and Lakshmana, by what strength could I dare protect the kingdom?
ramayana-2-67-11.meaning: He cannot rule without his brothers.
ramayana-2-67-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-12.translation: The mighty, righteous great king always relied on that strong one, as Mount Meru relies on its forest.
ramayana-2-67-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-13.translation: How can I, like an untrained bullock put to a yoke meant for a great ox, bear this burden? With what strength?
ramayana-2-67-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-14.translation: Or even if I had the strength, by means or by intelligence, I will not fulfil your wish, greedy for your son. I will bring my brother, dear to his people, back from the forest.
ramayana-2-67-14.meaning: He resolves to bring Rama home.
ramayana-2-67-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-67-15.translation: Having said this, great-souled Bharata, wounding her with many unkind words, roared again in grief like a lion in a mountain cave.
ramayana-2-67-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 67: Bharata, horrified, reproaches Kaikeyi and vows to bring Rama back from the forest rather than accept a throne won this way.

ramayana-2-68-1.translation: Having reproached his mother so, Bharata, filled with great anger, spoke again.
ramayana-2-68-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-2.translation: Fall from the kingdom, Kaikeyi, cruel, wicked woman! Abandoned by dharma, do not weep for the dead.
ramayana-2-68-2.meaning: He disowns her claim to power.
ramayana-2-68-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-3.translation: What wrong did the king or the deeply righteous Rama do you, that death and exile came to them equally because of you?
ramayana-2-68-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-4.translation: By destroying this family you have incurred the sin of killing the innocent. Kaikeyi, go to hell, and not to your husband's world.

ramayana-2-68-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-5.translation: By the sin you have committed through this terrible deed, abandoning him whom all the world loves, you have brought fear on me too.
ramayana-2-68-5.meaning: Her act endangers his reputation as well.
ramayana-2-68-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. ramayana-2-68-7.translation: Enemy in the shape of a mother, cruel, greedy for the kingdom, wicked, killer of your husband, I will not speak to you.

He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. ramayana-2-68-12.translation: Having separated righteous Kausalya from her son, set on evil, what world will you reach now, bound for hell?

ramayana-2-68-13.translation: Cruel one, do you not understand that Rama, Kausalya's own son, the eldest, like a father, is the steady refuge of his kin?

ramayana-2-68-14.translation: A son is born from every limb and from the heart. So he is dearer to his mother; through love, no kinsman is so dear.

ramayana-2-68-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. ramayana-2-68-18.translation: Seeing the glorious one burning with grief, Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, king of the gods, alarmed, folded his hands and spoke.

He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-19.translation: Is there some great danger to us from anywhere? Why are you grieving? Tell me, you who wish all beings well.

He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. ramayana-2-68-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-21.translation: Lord of immortals, may no harm come to you from anywhere. I grieve for my two sons who have sunk into hardship.

ramayana-2-68-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. ramayana-2-68-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-23.translation: Born from my body, suffering and crushed by burdens, seeing them I am tormented. Nothing is as dear as a son.
ramayana-2-68-23.meaning: Nothing compares to a parent's love for a child.
ramayana-2-68-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-24.translation: If she who grants all wishes and has thousands of sons still grieves, how will Kausalya live without Rama?
ramayana-2-68-24.meaning: If Surabhi grieves for two of many, think of Kausalya with her one son.
ramayana-2-68-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. He tells the story of Surabhi, the divine mother of cows, who wept to see her sons the oxen suffering under the plough, to show how deep a mother's love is and how Kaikeyi has wounded Kausalya. He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

He vows to bring Rama back. His harsh words are the outburst of a grieving son and are not presented as the epic's last word on Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-68-26.translation: I will without doubt make full amends to my brother and my father and increase their honour.

ramayana-2-68-29.meaning: He lies on the ground like a lowered flag.
ramayana-2-68-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 68: Bharata's anger continues. ramayana-2-69-1.translation: Hearing great-souled Bharata crying out like this, Kausalya said this to Sumitra.
ramayana-2-69-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-2.translation: Bharata, the son of cruel Kaikeyi, has come. I want to see far-sighted Bharata.

Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-17.translation: May the sin of those who betray a king who protects all beings like his children fall on him by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-17.meaning: Betraying a good ruler is a serious sin.
ramayana-2-69-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-18.translation: Whatever wrong a king commits who takes a sixth of the produce as tax yet does not protect his people, may that be his, by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-18.meaning: A ruler who taxes but does not protect betrays his people.
ramayana-2-69-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-19.translation: May the sin of those who promise sacrificial fees to ascetics at a ceremony and then deny them fall on him by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

of those who go back on their word

ramayana-2-69-20.translation: In battle crowded with elephants, horses and chariots and full of weapons, may he not follow the code of the good, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-21.translation: May that wicked one destroy the subtle teaching carefully taught by a wise teacher, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-21.meaning: Wasting or betraying knowledge is a wrong.
ramayana-2-69-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-22.translation: May he, heartless, eat rice pudding, sesame rice and goat's meat for no sacred purpose, and may he insult his elders, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-22.meaning: Selfishness and disrespect to elders are condemned.
ramayana-2-69-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-23.translation: Surrounded by sons, wives and servants in his own house, may he eat fine food alone, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-23.meaning: Not sharing food with one's household is selfish.
ramayana-2-69-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-24.translation: May he incur the sin said to belong to killing a king, a woman, a child or an old person, and the sin of abandoning dependants.
ramayana-2-69-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-25.translation: Whatever sin is held to fall on one who sleeps at both twilights, may that sin be his, by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-25.meaning: Neglecting daily duties was seen as a fault.
ramayana-2-69-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-26.translation: May he incur the sin of an arsonist, the sin of one who violates his teacher's bed, and the sin of betraying a friend.
ramayana-2-69-26.meaning: Betrayal of trust is among the worst wrongs.
ramayana-2-69-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-27.translation: May he never serve the gods, the ancestors, or his mother and father, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-27.meaning: Failing to honour parents and ancestors is condemned.
ramayana-2-69-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-28.translation: May he quickly, this very day, fall from the world of the good, from the fame of the good, and from deeds the good practise, he by whose consent the noble one went.
ramayana-2-69-28.meaning: He wishes total disgrace on whoever caused the exile.
ramayana-2-69-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

keywords.meaning: he by whose consent the noble one went

ramayana-2-69-29.translation: Comforting Kausalya, bereft of husband and son, in this way, the prince, overcome by sorrow, fell down.
ramayana-2-69-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-30.translation: As Bharata, burning with grief, lay senseless, swearing such grievous oaths, Kausalya spoke to him.
ramayana-2-69-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-31.translation: Son, this sorrow of mine grows even more, for by swearing these oaths you choke my very breath.
ramayana-2-69-31.meaning: She cannot bear to see him suffer so.
ramayana-2-69-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-32.translation: Thank goodness your heart, like Lakshmana's, has not swerved from dharma. Child, true to your word, you will reach the worlds of the good.
ramayana-2-69-32.meaning: She accepts his innocence and blesses him.
ramayana-2-69-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-33.translation: As the great-souled one lamented, stricken with sorrow, his mind was shaken by confusion and the weight of grief.
ramayana-2-69-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-69-34.translation: As he lay on the ground, lamenting over and over, senseless, his mind lost, sighing long and often, that night passed in grief.
ramayana-2-69-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 69: Kausalya, suspecting Bharata had a hand in the exile, speaks bitterly to him. Bharata answers with a long series of oaths: may whoever approved of Rama's exile bear the guilt of every kind of wrongdoing. The list is a window into the moral code of the time. Kausalya is convinced of his innocence and embraces him.

ramayana-2-70-1.translation: To Bharata, Kaikeyi's son, burning with grief, Vasishtha, best of speakers, the sage of fine words, spoke.
ramayana-2-70-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-2.translation: Enough of grief, may you be well, famous prince. Perform the king's final journey, which is now due.
ramayana-2-70-2.meaning: It is time for the funeral.
ramayana-2-70-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-3.translation: Hearing Vasishtha's words, Bharata steadied himself and, knowing dharma, had all the funeral rites performed.
ramayana-2-70-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-4.translation: The king was taken out of the oil and laid on the ground, his face yellowish, as though asleep.
ramayana-2-70-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-5.translation: Laying him on a fine bed adorned with many jewels, his son, deeply grieved, lamented over Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-70-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-6.translation: King, what did you decide while I was away and had not returned, having exiled righteous Rama and mighty Lakshmana?
ramayana-2-70-6.meaning: He wonders what his father intended.
ramayana-2-70-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-7.translation: Where will you go, great king, leaving these grieving people, without Rama, the lion among men, tireless in deeds?
ramayana-2-70-7.meaning: Who will care for the people now?
ramayana-2-70-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-8.translation: King, father, who will provide for the welfare and safety of this city now that you have gone to heaven and Rama has gone to the forest?
ramayana-2-70-8.meaning: The kingdom is without a guardian.
ramayana-2-70-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-9.translation: King, the earth, widowed without you, does not shine. The city seems to me like a night without the moon.
ramayana-2-70-9.meaning: The land has lost its lord.
ramayana-2-70-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-10.translation: As Bharata lamented thus, sad at heart, the great sage Vasishtha spoke to him again.
ramayana-2-70-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-11.translation: Mighty-armed one, let the funeral rites due to this lord of the people be done calmly and without hesitation.
ramayana-2-70-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-12.translation: Saying 'So be it' and honouring Vasishtha's words, Bharata hurried all the officiating priests, royal priests and teachers.
ramayana-2-70-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-13.translation: The king's sacred fires, brought out of the fire-house, were carried ahead by the priests and sacrificers according to the rules.
ramayana-2-70-13.meaning: The sacred fires lead the procession.
ramayana-2-70-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-14.translation: Then the attendants, choked with tears and heavy-hearted, placed the lifeless king on a palanquin and carried him.
ramayana-2-70-14.meaning: The king's body is carried out.
ramayana-2-70-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-15.translation: People went ahead of the king, scattering silver, gold and many kinds of cloth along the road.
ramayana-2-70-15.meaning: Gifts are scattered along the way.
ramayana-2-70-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-16.translation: Others brought sandalwood, aloe resin, sarala, padmaka and deodar wood and built the pyre.
ramayana-2-70-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-17.translation: After placing many kinds of fragrant substances there, the priests laid the king in the middle of the pyre.
ramayana-2-70-17.meaning: The king is laid on the pyre.
ramayana-2-70-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-18.translation: Offering into the fire, his priests murmured prayers, and the Sama chanters sang Sama hymns there as the scriptures direct.
ramayana-2-70-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-19.translation: The king's wives, in palanquins and carriages as befitted them, left the city then, surrounded by elders.
ramayana-2-70-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-20.translation: The priests and the grieving women, led by Kausalya, walked around the king on the pyre, keeping it to their left.
ramayana-2-70-20.meaning: They circle the pyre in the funeral manner.
ramayana-2-70-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Vasishtha urges Bharata to perform his father's funeral. Dasharatha's body is taken from the oil, laid on a fine bier and carried to the cremation ground, where the priests perform the rites.

ramayana-2-70-21.translation: There the cry of the women was heard, like that of krauncha birds, thousands of them crying out pitifully in their distress.
ramayana-2-70-21.meaning: The women's wailing fills the air.
ramayana-2-70-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Dasharatha is cremated by the Sarayu. The royal women lament, and the family spends ten days of mourning.

ramayana-2-70-22.translation: Then the noble women, weeping helplessly and lamenting again and again, came down from their carriages to the bank of the Sarayu.
ramayana-2-70-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Dasharatha is cremated by the Sarayu. The royal women lament, and the family spends ten days of mourning.

ramayana-2-70-23.translation: Having offered water with Bharata, the royal women, ministers and priests entered the city, their eyes filled with tears, and spent ten days in grief, sleeping on the ground.
ramayana-2-70-23.meaning: The family keeps ten days of mourning.
ramayana-2-70-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 70: Dasharatha is cremated by the Sarayu. The royal women lament, and the family spends ten days of mourning.

ramayana-2-71-1.translation: When the ten days had passed and he had been purified, on the twelfth day the prince had the shraddha rites performed.
ramayana-2-71-1.meaning: Bharata performs the rites for the dead.
ramayana-2-71-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-2.translation: He gave the Brahmins jewels, wealth and plenty of food, white goats in great number, and hundreds of cows.
ramayana-2-71-2.meaning: He gives generous gifts in his father's honour.
ramayana-2-71-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-3.translation: The king's son gave the Brahmins servants, carriages and very large houses for the king's welfare after death.
ramayana-2-71-3.meaning: Charity is offered for the departed.
ramayana-2-71-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-4.translation: Then at dawn on the thirteenth day, mighty-armed Bharata, overcome by grief, lamented.
ramayana-2-71-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-5.translation: His throat choked so he could hardly speak, he came to gather the remains, and at the foot of his father's pyre he said in deep sorrow:
ramayana-2-71-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-6.translation: Father, my brother Raghava, to whom you entrusted me, has gone to the forest, and I am left alone and abandoned by you.
ramayana-2-71-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-7.translation: Her son, the refuge of the helpless, has been banished to the forest. Where have you gone, king, leaving mother Kausalya?
ramayana-2-71-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-8.translation: Seeing the ash-red circle of burnt bones where his father's body had been consumed, he groaned and sank down.
ramayana-2-71-8.meaning: The sight of the ashes overwhelms him.
ramayana-2-71-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-9.translation: Seeing it, weeping and wretched, he fell to the ground like Indra's banner falling while being raised.
ramayana-2-71-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-10.translation: Then all his ministers ran to him, pure in his vows, as the sages ran to Yayati when he fell at the end of his merit.
ramayana-2-71-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-11.translation: Shatrughna too, seeing Bharata flooded with grief, fell senseless to the ground, remembering the king.
ramayana-2-71-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-12.translation: As if mad and senseless, he lamented in deep sorrow, remembering his father's many virtues one by one.
ramayana-2-71-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-13.translation: This fierce ocean of sorrow, rising from Manthara, full of the crocodile Kaikeyi, made of the granting of boons and impossible to stir, has drowned us.
ramayana-2-71-13.meaning: He likens their grief to an ocean.
ramayana-2-71-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-14.translation: Father, where have you gone, leaving lamenting Bharata, tender and young, whom you always pampered?
ramayana-2-71-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-15.translation: Did you not offer all of us food, drink, clothes and ornaments? Who will do that for us now?
ramayana-2-71-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-16.translation: At this time when it should break apart, the earth does not split, though it has lost you, the great-souled king who knew dharma.
ramayana-2-71-16.meaning: He is amazed the world carries on.
ramayana-2-71-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-17.translation: With my father gone to heaven and Rama in the forest, what power do I have to live? I will enter the fire.
ramayana-2-71-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-18.translation: Bereft of my brother and father, I will not enter empty Ayodhya, ruled by the Ikshvakus; I will enter a forest of austerity.
ramayana-2-71-18.meaning: He would rather become a hermit.
ramayana-2-71-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-19.translation: Hearing their lament and seeing the disaster, all the followers were even more stricken.
ramayana-2-71-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-20.translation: Then Shatrughna and Bharata, both dejected and exhausted, writhed on the ground like two bulls with broken horns.
ramayana-2-71-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-21.translation: Then Vasishtha, their father's priest, steady in nature and wise, raised Bharata and spoke to him.
ramayana-2-71-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-22.translation: Three pairs of opposites act on all beings without distinction. Since they cannot be avoided, you should not behave like this.
ramayana-2-71-22.meaning: Hunger and thirst, grief and confusion, old age and death come to everyone; accept them calmly.
ramayana-2-71-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-23.translation: Sumantra, who knew the truth, raised and calmed Shatrughna and told him about the arising and passing away of all beings.
ramayana-2-71-23.meaning: Sumantra reminds him everything born must pass.
ramayana-2-71-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-24.translation: Raised up, those two famous tigers among men shone like two of Indra's banners soaked by rain and sun.
ramayana-2-71-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-71-25.translation: As they wiped their tears, red-eyed and speaking sadly, the ministers urged the two sons to perform the remaining rites.
ramayana-2-71-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 71: After the days of impurity, Bharata performs the shraddha rites and gives generous gifts. At the cremation ground he and Shatrughna break down in grief, and Vasishtha and Sumantra remind them that all beings face birth and death, gain and loss, pleasure and pain.

ramayana-2-72-1.translation: As Bharata, burning with grief, was planning to set out, Shatrughna, Lakshmana's younger brother, said this to him.
ramayana-2-72-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-2.translation: Rama, full of goodness, who is the refuge of all beings in sorrow, let alone his own family, has been sent to the forest by a woman.
ramayana-2-72-2.meaning: He is outraged that Rama was exiled.
ramayana-2-72-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-3.translation: And that strong, brave one called Lakshmana, why did he not free Rama, even by restraining our father?
ramayana-2-72-3.meaning: He wonders why Lakshmana did not act.
ramayana-2-72-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-4.translation: The king should have been restrained from the start, considering right and wrong policy, when he took the wrong path and fell under a woman's control.
ramayana-2-72-4.meaning: He thinks Dasharatha should have been stopped.
ramayana-2-72-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-5.translation: As Shatrughna was speaking, the hunchbacked woman appeared at the eastern gate, adorned with all her ornaments.
ramayana-2-72-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-6.translation: She was smeared with fine sandal paste and wore royal clothes, decorated with colourful girdles and strings.
ramayana-2-72-6.meaning: She is dressed in finery while the palace mourns.
ramayana-2-72-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-7.translation: Seeing her who had done such great wrong, the gatekeeper seized the hunchbacked woman roughly and handed her over to Shatrughna.
ramayana-2-72-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-8.translation: 'Here is the wicked, cruel woman because of whom Rama is in the forest and your father has given up his body. Do with her as you think fit.'
ramayana-2-72-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-9.translation: Hearing those words, Shatrughna, deeply grieved and firm in his vows, said this to all the palace attendants.
ramayana-2-72-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-10.translation: Let her who caused such sharp pain to my brothers and my father taste the fruit of her cruel deed.
ramayana-2-72-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-11.translation: Having said this, he quickly seized the hunchbacked woman by force among her companions, and she made the house ring with her cries.
ramayana-2-72-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-12.translation: Then all her companions, greatly distressed, seeing Shatrughna's anger, fled in every direction.
ramayana-2-72-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-13.translation: All her companions conferred together: 'The way he has started, he will destroy us completely.'
ramayana-2-72-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-14.translation: 'Let us take refuge with Kausalya, who is compassionate, generous, righteous and famous. She will surely be our refuge.'
ramayana-2-72-14.meaning: They trust Kausalya's kindness even now.
ramayana-2-72-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-15.translation: Shatrughna, scorcher of foes, his eyes red with fury, then dragged the screaming hunchbacked woman along the ground.
ramayana-2-72-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-16.translation: As Manthara was dragged here and there, her many colourful ornaments scattered on the ground.
ramayana-2-72-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-17.translation: Strewn with those ornaments, the splendid royal palace shone like the autumn sky.
ramayana-2-72-17.meaning: The scattered jewels glitter like stars.
ramayana-2-72-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-18.translation: That strong bull among men, holding her firmly in his anger, rebuked Kaikeyi and spoke harsh words to her.
ramayana-2-72-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.
