ramayana-2-72-19.translation: Deeply pained by those harsh and hurtful words, Kaikeyi, terrified of Shatrughna, ran to her son for refuge.
ramayana-2-72-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-20.translation: Seeing her, Bharata said to the angry Shatrughna: 'Women are not to be killed by any being. Let her be forgiven.'
ramayana-2-72-20.meaning: Bharata insists on restraint and mercy.
ramayana-2-72-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-21.translation: I would kill this wicked, ill-behaved Kaikeyi myself, if righteous Rama would not despise me as a matricide.
ramayana-2-72-21.meaning: Respect for Rama's values holds him back.
ramayana-2-72-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-22.translation: If Raghava knew that even this hunchbacked woman had been killed, the righteous one would surely never speak to you or me again.
ramayana-2-72-22.meaning: Rama would never accept such revenge.
ramayana-2-72-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-23.translation: Hearing Bharata's words, Shatrughna, Lakshmana's younger brother, turned away from his anger and released Manthara.
ramayana-2-72-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-24.translation: Manthara fell at Kaikeyi's feet, sighing, in great distress, and lamented pitifully.
ramayana-2-72-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-72-25.translation: Seeing the hunchbacked woman, dazed from Shatrughna's rough handling and in distress, Bharata's mother gently comforted her, looking at her like a trapped krauncha bird.
ramayana-2-72-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 72: Shatrughna, angry, seizes Manthara when she appears in finery. Bharata stops him, saying women must not be killed and that Rama would never forgive such an act. The descriptions of Manthara's body are the narrator's of the time; the lesson of the scene is Bharata's restraint.

ramayana-2-73-1.translation: Then at dawn on the fourteenth day the king-makers gathered and spoke to Bharata.
ramayana-2-73-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-2.translation: Dasharatha, our most revered elder, has gone to heaven, having exiled the eldest, Rama, and mighty Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-73-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-3.translation: Famous prince, be our king today. Then this leaderless kingdom will come to no harm.
ramayana-2-73-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-4.translation: Raghava, your kinsmen and the guilds are waiting for you, prince, with everything ready for the consecration.
ramayana-2-73-4.meaning: All is ready for the coronation.
ramayana-2-73-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-5.translation: Bharata, take the great kingdom of your fathers and grandfathers. Have yourself consecrated and protect us, bull among men.
ramayana-2-73-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-6.translation: Walking reverently around all the consecration items, Bharata, firm in his vows, replied to all the people.
ramayana-2-73-6.meaning: He honours the items but declines.
ramayana-2-73-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-7.translation: In our family the kingship has always belonged to the eldest. You good people should not speak to me like this.
ramayana-2-73-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-8.translation: Rama, our elder brother, will be lord of the earth. I will live in the forest for fourteen years.
ramayana-2-73-8.meaning: He offers to take Rama's place in exile.
ramayana-2-73-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-9.translation: Let a great army with its four divisions be readied. I will bring my eldest brother Raghava back from the forest.
ramayana-2-73-9.meaning: He prepares to bring Rama home.
ramayana-2-73-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-10.translation: Taking all these prepared consecration items ahead, I will go to the forest for Rama's sake.
ramayana-2-73-10.meaning: He will carry the coronation to Rama.
ramayana-2-73-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-11.translation: There I will consecrate that tiger among men and bring Rama back, honoured before all, as the sacred fire is brought from the sacrifice.
ramayana-2-73-11.meaning: He will crown Rama in the forest itself.
ramayana-2-73-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-12.translation: I will not fulfil the wish of this woman who is my mother only in name. I will live in the hard forest; Rama will be king.
ramayana-2-73-12.meaning: He rejects his mother's plan entirely.
ramayana-2-73-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-13.translation: Let craftsmen make a road, levelling the uneven places, and let guards who scout difficult terrain go along the road.
ramayana-2-73-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-14.translation: As the prince spoke thus for Rama's sake, all the people replied with these excellent, auspicious words.
ramayana-2-73-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-15.translation: Since you, speaking so, wish to give the earth to the eldest prince, may lotus-dwelling Lakshmi, goddess of fortune, wait upon you.
ramayana-2-73-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-16.translation: Hearing those excellent words of the prince, tears of joy fell from the noble people's eyes.
ramayana-2-73-16.meaning: His decision brings tears of joy.
ramayana-2-73-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-73-17.translation: Hearing this, the ministers and the assembly, their grief gone, said joyfully: 'At your command the people, devoted to the best of men, and the craftsmen have been ordered to build the road.'
ramayana-2-73-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 73: On the fourteenth day the king-makers ask Bharata to accept the throne. He refuses, saying the kingship belongs to the eldest, Rama, and orders an army and road-builders to prepare to go and bring Rama back. The people weep for joy.

ramayana-2-74-1.translation: Then those who knew the land, experts in measuring with cords, devoted to their work, brave diggers and engineers...
ramayana-2-74-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-2.translation: ...overseers, architects, men skilled with machines, carpenters, road-makers and woodcutters...
ramayana-2-74-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-3.translation: ...well-diggers, plasterers, bamboo-workers and capable supervisors went on ahead.
ramayana-2-74-3.meaning: The work crews lead the way.
ramayana-2-74-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-4.translation: That vast crowd of people moving joyfully towards that place looked like the great surge of the ocean at the full moon.
ramayana-2-74-4.meaning: The crowd moves like a tide.
ramayana-2-74-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-5.translation: Those experts in road-building, each in his group, set out ahead with all kinds of tools.
ramayana-2-74-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-6.translation: Clearing creepers, vines, bushes, stumps and stones, and cutting many kinds of trees, the people made the road.
ramayana-2-74-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-7.translation: Where there were no trees, some planted trees; others cut here and there with axes, chisels and sickles.
ramayana-2-74-7.meaning: They plant as well as clear.
ramayana-2-74-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-8.translation: Other very strong men cleared clumps of virana grass and levelled rough places and mounds here and there.
ramayana-2-74-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-9.translation: Others filled wells and long pits with earth, and some levelled the low places all around.
ramayana-2-74-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-10.translation: Then the men bridged what needed bridging, crushed what needed crushing and broke through what needed breaking, in various places.
ramayana-2-74-10.meaning: Bridges are built and obstacles removed.
ramayana-2-74-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-11.translation: In a short time they made many channels full of water, of many shapes, like seas, and many kinds of wells adorned with platforms.
ramayana-2-74-11.meaning: Water supplies are created along the way.
ramayana-2-74-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-12.translation: With floors paved with plaster, flowering trees, flocks of excited birds singing, and decorated with banners...
ramayana-2-74-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-13.translation: ...sprinkled with sandal water and adorned with many flowers, the army's road shone greatly, like the road to heaven.
ramayana-2-74-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-14.translation: Then the officers in charge, as ordered, in pleasant places with many sweet fruits...
ramayana-2-74-14.meaning: Camps are prepared in good spots.
ramayana-2-74-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-15.translation: ...decorated even more with ornaments the camp intended for great-souled Bharata, already like an ornament itself.
ramayana-2-74-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-16.translation: Experts set up great-souled Bharata's camp under favourable stars and at auspicious moments.
ramayana-2-74-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-17.translation: With many earth ramparts, surrounded by moats, like Indra's pillar, adorned with fine gateways...
ramayana-2-74-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-18.translation: ...with rows of mansions, enclosed by white walls, all decorated with banners, with well-made main roads...
ramayana-2-74-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-19.translation: ...with tall towers rising as if spreading into the sky, those camps shone like Indra's city.
ramayana-2-74-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-20.translation: Reaching the Ganga, with forests of many trees, cool and clear water, and full of great fish...
ramayana-2-74-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: Skilled workers of every kind go ahead to build a fine road and camps for Bharata's march to the forest, clearing land, filling hollows and digging wells.

ramayana-2-74-21.translation: As the clear night sky shines adorned with the moon and hosts of stars, so the lovely royal road, built by fine craftsmen, shone more and more.
ramayana-2-74-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 74: The road for Bharata's march is finished, beautiful and well built.

ramayana-2-75-1.translation: Then, on the night before the auspicious ceremony, bards and heralds skilled in fine speech praised Bharata with auspicious hymns.
ramayana-2-75-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-2.translation: The watch drum, struck with golden sticks, sounded; they blew hundreds of conches and instruments of high and low pitch.
ramayana-2-75-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-3.translation: That great sound of instruments, filling the sky as it were, pierced grief-stricken Bharata with sorrow again.
ramayana-2-75-3.meaning: The celebration only deepens his grief.
ramayana-2-75-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-4.translation: Then, waking, Bharata stopped the sound, saying 'I am not the king,' and spoke to Shatrughna.
ramayana-2-75-4.meaning: He refuses to be hailed as king.
ramayana-2-75-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-5.translation: See, Shatrughna, the great harm Kaikeyi has done the world. King Dasharatha has gone, leaving his sorrows to me.
ramayana-2-75-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-6.translation: The royal fortune of that great-souled king of dharma, rooted in dharma, drifts about like a boat without a helmsman on the water.
ramayana-2-75-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-7.translation: Seeing Bharata lamenting senselessly, all the women wept aloud pitifully.
ramayana-2-75-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-8.translation: While he was lamenting, famous Vasishtha, who knew the duties of kings, entered the assembly hall of the Ikshvaku lord.
ramayana-2-75-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-9.translation: The righteous one with his followers came to the lovely golden hall, full of gems and jewels, like Sudharma, the hall of the gods.
ramayana-2-75-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-10.translation: He, who knew all the Vedas, sat on a golden seat covered with a costly cloth and instructed the messengers.
ramayana-2-75-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-11.translation: Calmly and quickly bring the Brahmins, warriors, soldiers, ministers and leaders of groups, for we have urgent business.
ramayana-2-75-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-12.translation: Then a great tumult arose as people came by chariots, horses and elephants.
ramayana-2-75-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-13.translation: Then the people welcomed Bharata as he came, as the gods welcome Indra, just as they had welcomed Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-75-13.meaning: He is welcomed like his father.
ramayana-2-75-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-75-14.translation: Like a lake full of great fish and serpents, with still water and gems, shells and sand, the hall graced by Dasharatha's son shone as it did before with Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-75-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 75: At dawn bards and drums hail Bharata as king. He stops them, saying 'I am not the king.' Vasishtha calls an assembly of Brahmins, warriors, ministers and leaders.

ramayana-2-76-1.translation: Wise Bharata saw the assembly, full of nobles and well ordered, like a night with a full moon.
ramayana-2-76-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-2.translation: As the nobles took their seats in proper order, it looked like a night with a full moon after the clouds have gone.
ramayana-2-76-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-3.translation: Seeing all the king's subjects assembled, the royal priest, who knew dharma, spoke gently to Bharata.
ramayana-2-76-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-4.translation: Dear one, King Dasharatha has gone to heaven after living by dharma, having given you the prosperous earth rich in wealth and grain.
ramayana-2-76-4.meaning: The king left the realm to Bharata.
ramayana-2-76-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-5.translation: Rama too, firm in truth, remembering the dharma of the good, did not abandon his father's command, as the rising moon does not give up its light.
ramayana-2-76-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-6.translation: The kingdom given to you by your father and brother is free of enemies. Enjoy it with your ministers glad, and have yourself consecrated quickly.
ramayana-2-76-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-7.translation: Let the kings of the north, west and south, and of the far frontier and the coasts, bring you jewels.
ramayana-2-76-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-8.translation: Hearing this, Bharata, flooded with grief, his mind went to Rama, knowing dharma and wishing to follow it.
ramayana-2-76-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-9.translation: The young man, with a voice like a swan's but choked with tears, lamented in the middle of the assembly and rebuked the priest.
ramayana-2-76-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-10.translation: Who like me would take the kingdom of one who has lived the student's life, completed his learning, is wise and strives in dharma?
ramayana-2-76-10.meaning: He will not take Rama's place.
ramayana-2-76-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-11.translation: How could one born of Dasharatha steal a kingdom? The kingdom and I both belong to Rama. You should speak of dharma here.
ramayana-2-76-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-12.translation: The eldest and best, righteous, like Dilipa and Nahusha, Kakutstha deserves to have the kingdom as Dasharatha did.
ramayana-2-76-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-13.translation: If I did this sinful thing, practised by the ignoble and not leading to heaven, I would be the disgrace of the Ikshvaku family in the world.
ramayana-2-76-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-14.translation: I do not approve of the sin my mother committed. Standing here, I bow with folded hands to him who lives in the hard forest.
ramayana-2-76-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-15.translation: I will follow Rama. He is the king, the best of men. Raghava deserves the kingdom of all three worlds.
ramayana-2-76-15.meaning: Rama is worthy of every honour.
ramayana-2-76-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-16.translation: Hearing those words full of dharma, all the members of the assembly, their hearts set on Rama, shed tears of joy.
ramayana-2-76-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-17.translation: If I cannot bring my noble brother back from the forest, I will live there in the forest, as noble Lakshmana does.
ramayana-2-76-17.meaning: He will join Rama if he cannot bring him back.
ramayana-2-76-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-18.translation: I will use every means to bring him back by force of persuasion, in the presence of the noble, the good and the virtuous.
ramayana-2-76-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-19.translation: Having said this, righteous Bharata, loving towards his brother, spoke to Sumantra, skilled in counsel, who stood near.
ramayana-2-76-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-20.translation: Rise quickly, Sumantra, and go at my command. Order the march at once and gather the army.
ramayana-2-76-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-21.translation: Told this by great-souled Bharata, Sumantra, delighted, ordered everything as instructed, as he wished.
ramayana-2-76-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-22.translation: The people and the army commanders were delighted to hear that the march to bring Raghava back had been ordered.
ramayana-2-76-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-23.translation: Then in every house the soldiers' wives, hearing of the march, joyfully hurried their husbands.
ramayana-2-76-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-24.translation: The army commanders with the soldiers urged on the whole army, with horses, swift ox-carts and chariots fast as thought.
ramayana-2-76-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-25.translation: Seeing the army ready, Bharata, in the presence of his elders, said to Sumantra at his side, 'Hurry my chariot.'
ramayana-2-76-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-26.translation: Accepting Bharata's command with delight, he took the chariot yoked with the finest horses and set out.
ramayana-2-76-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-27.translation: Then Bharata, of the Raghu line, steadfast in truth, powerful, firm and true in valour, intending to win the favour of his famous elder gone to the great forest, spoke.
ramayana-2-76-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-28.translation: Rise quickly, Sumantra, and go to the army chiefs to assemble the army. I wish to win over Rama in the forest and bring him back for the good of the world.
ramayana-2-76-28.meaning: His aim is the world's welfare.
ramayana-2-76-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-29.translation: The charioteer's son, properly commanded by Bharata and with his wish fulfilled, instructed all the leaders of the people, the army chiefs and the friends.
ramayana-2-76-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-76-30.translation: Then in every family, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, Shudras and Brahmins rose and yoked camel-carts, mules, elephants and well-bred horses.
ramayana-2-76-30.meaning: People of every class join the march.
ramayana-2-76-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 76: In the assembly Vasishtha offers Bharata the throne. Bharata refuses in tears, says the kingdom belongs to Rama, and vows to bring him back or else live in the forest himself. He orders the army and the people to prepare to march.

ramayana-2-77-1.translation: Then rising early and mounting the finest chariot, Bharata set out quickly, longing to see Rama.
ramayana-2-77-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-2.translation: Ahead of him went all the ministers and priests, riding chariots drawn by horses, like the sun's chariot.
ramayana-2-77-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-3.translation: Nine thousand elephants, properly equipped, followed Bharata, the joy of the Ikshvaku family, as he went.
ramayana-2-77-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-4.translation: Sixty thousand chariots with archers bearing various weapons followed the famous prince Bharata as he went.
ramayana-2-77-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-5.translation: A hundred thousand horses with riders followed the famous prince Bharata, of the Raghu line, as he went.
ramayana-2-77-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-6.translation: Kaikeyi, Sumitra and famous Kausalya went in a shining carriage, delighted at the prospect of bringing Rama back.
ramayana-2-77-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-7.translation: Groups of nobles set out to see Rama with Lakshmana, telling delightful stories about him, their hearts glad.
ramayana-2-77-7.meaning: People share stories of Rama on the way.
ramayana-2-77-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-8.translation: When will we see Rama, dark as a rain cloud, mighty-armed, steady in nature, firm in his vows, who drives away the world's sorrow?
ramayana-2-77-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-9.translation: As soon as he is seen, Raghava will take away our grief, as the rising sun dispels the darkness of the whole world.
ramayana-2-77-9.meaning: Seeing Rama will end their sorrow.
ramayana-2-77-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-10.translation: Telling such happy, auspicious stories and embracing one another, the citizens went on.
ramayana-2-77-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-11.translation: All the other respected people there and the merchants, all the people, went joyfully towards Rama.
ramayana-2-77-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-12.translation: Some jewellers, fine potters, weavers and those who live by weapons...
ramayana-2-77-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-13.translation: ...makers of peacock-feather goods, sawyers, decorators, borers, ivory-workers, plasterers and perfumers...
ramayana-2-77-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-14.translation: ...famous goldsmiths, blanket-washers, bath attendants, physicians, incense-makers and brewers...
ramayana-2-77-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-15.translation: ...washermen, tailors, village and cowherd headmen, and actors with their women, and fishermen too went.
ramayana-2-77-15.meaning: The whole community joins the march.
ramayana-2-77-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-16.translation: Thousands of composed, Veda-knowing Brahmins of respected conduct followed Bharata in ox-carts.
ramayana-2-77-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-17.translation: All of them, well dressed in clean clothes and anointed with copper-coloured paste, followed Bharata slowly in various vehicles.
ramayana-2-77-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-18.translation: The joyful, delighted army followed Kaikeyi's son, and that army following Bharata halted.
ramayana-2-77-18.meaning: The march comes to a halt.
ramayana-2-77-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-19.translation: Looking at the army following him and at the Ganga with its auspicious water, Bharata, skilled in speech, spoke to all his ministers.
ramayana-2-77-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-20.translation: Settle my army as you see fit. After resting, we will cross the great river tomorrow.
ramayana-2-77-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-21.translation: Meanwhile I wish to go down to the river and offer water for the welfare of the king who has gone to heaven.
ramayana-2-77-21.meaning: He makes a water offering for his father.
ramayana-2-77-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-22.translation: As he said this, the ministers attentively said 'So be it' and settled the troops, each where they wished.
ramayana-2-77-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-77-23.translation: Having camped the army, splendid with its equipment, along the great Ganga, Bharata stayed there, thinking about how to bring back great-souled Rama.
ramayana-2-77-23.meaning: He thinks of how to bring Rama home.
ramayana-2-77-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 77: Bharata sets out with a vast army, the three queens, priests and people of every trade, all longing to see Rama. They camp on the bank of the Ganga.

ramayana-2-78-1.translation: Then the king of the Nishadas, seeing the army camped along the Ganga, quickly spoke to his kinsmen.
ramayana-2-78-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-2.translation: This army looks huge, like an ocean. Even thinking hard, I cannot see its end.
ramayana-2-78-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-3.translation: That great one with the kovidara banner on his chariot will either have us boatmen bound or kill us.
ramayana-2-78-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-4.translation: Or Bharata, Kaikeyi's son, is coming to kill Rama, son of Dasharatha, exiled from the kingdom by his father.
ramayana-2-78-4.meaning: He suspects Bharata means Rama harm.
ramayana-2-78-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-5.translation: Rama, son of Dasharatha, is my lord and my friend. For his sake stand ready here in armour on the banks of the Ganga.
ramayana-2-78-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-6.translation: Let all the boatmen stand along the Ganga, guarding the river with forces, living on meat, roots and fruit.
ramayana-2-78-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-7.translation: He ordered five hundred boats, each with a hundred young armed fishermen, to stand ready.
ramayana-2-78-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-8.translation: If Bharata is well disposed towards Rama here, this army will cross the Ganga safely today.
ramayana-2-78-8.meaning: He will help if Bharata's intent is good.
ramayana-2-78-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-9.translation: Saying this, Guha, lord of the Nishadas, took gifts of fish, meat and honey and approached Bharata.
ramayana-2-78-9.meaning: He goes to meet Bharata with gifts.
ramayana-2-78-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-10.translation: Seeing him coming, the mighty charioteer's son, who knew courtesy, humbly told Bharata.
ramayana-2-78-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-11.translation: This chief, surrounded by a thousand kinsmen, knows the Dandaka forest well; he is elderly and your brother's friend.
ramayana-2-78-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-12.translation: So, Kakutstha, let Guha, lord of the Nishadas, see you. He certainly knows where Rama and Lakshmana are.
ramayana-2-78-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-13.translation: Hearing these good words from Sumantra, Bharata quickly said, 'Let Guha see me.'
ramayana-2-78-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-14.translation: Given permission, Guha, delighted and surrounded by kinsmen, came humbly to Bharata and spoke.
ramayana-2-78-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-15.translation: This land is your garden; you have caught us by surprise. We offer you everything; stay in your own boatmen's house.
ramayana-2-78-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-16.translation: There are roots and fruit gathered by the Nishadas, fresh and dried meat, and a great variety of forest food.
ramayana-2-78-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-78-17.translation: I hope the army will stay this night well fed. Honoured with all you wish, you will go with your troops tomorrow.
ramayana-2-78-17.meaning: He hopes Bharata will rest as his guest.
ramayana-2-78-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 78: Guha, king of the Nishadas and Rama's friend, sees the great army and fears Bharata means to harm Rama. He readies his boatmen, then goes to meet Bharata with gifts.

ramayana-2-79-1.translation: Addressed thus, the very wise Bharata replied to Guha, lord of the Nishadas, with reasonable words.
ramayana-2-79-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Bharata thanks Guha warmly and asks the way to Bharadvaja's hermitage.

ramayana-2-79-2.translation: Friend of my elder brother, your wish is generous indeed, that you alone want to honour such a large army.
ramayana-2-79-2.meaning: He thanks Guha for his generosity.
ramayana-2-79-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Bharata thanks Guha warmly and asks the way to Bharadvaja's hermitage.

ramayana-2-79-3.translation: Having said these excellent words to Guha, the splendid and glorious Bharata spoke again to the lord of the Nishadas.
ramayana-2-79-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Bharata thanks Guha warmly and asks the way to Bharadvaja's hermitage.

ramayana-2-79-4.translation: Guha, by which way shall I go to Bharadvaja's hermitage? This region along the Ganga is very dense and hard to cross.
ramayana-2-79-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Bharata thanks Guha warmly and asks the way to Bharadvaja's hermitage.

ramayana-2-79-5.translation: Hearing the words of the wise prince, Guha, who roamed the deep forest, folded his hands and spoke.
ramayana-2-79-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Bharata thanks Guha warmly and asks the way to Bharadvaja's hermitage.

ramayana-2-79-6.translation: The boatmen will go with you, armed and alert, and I will go with you too, famous prince.
ramayana-2-79-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-7.translation: I hope you are not going with ill intent toward Rama, tireless in deeds? This great army of yours makes me uneasy.
ramayana-2-79-7.meaning: Guha asks plainly about Bharata's intent.
ramayana-2-79-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-8.translation: As he spoke thus, Bharata, clear as the sky, answered Guha with gentle words.
ramayana-2-79-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-9.translation: May such a terrible time never come! You should not suspect me. Raghava is my eldest brother, like a father to me.
ramayana-2-79-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-10.translation: I am going to bring back Kakutstha, who lives in the forest. Do not think otherwise, Guha; I am telling you the truth.
ramayana-2-79-10.meaning: His only aim is to bring Rama home.
ramayana-2-79-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-11.translation: Hearing Bharata's words, Guha, his face glowing with joy, spoke again to Bharata, delighted.
ramayana-2-79-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-12.translation: You are blessed. I see no one equal to you on earth, since you wish to give up a kingdom that came to you without effort.
ramayana-2-79-12.meaning: Giving up power freely is rare and admirable.
ramayana-2-79-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-13.translation: Surely your fame will travel the worlds forever, since you want to bring back Rama, who is in difficulty.
ramayana-2-79-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-14.translation: As Guha was speaking to Bharata, the sun lost its light and night came on.
ramayana-2-79-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-15.translation: Having settled the army and been made welcome by Guha, glorious Bharata went to bed with Shatrughna.
ramayana-2-79-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-16.translation: Grief full of thoughts of Rama came upon great-souled Bharata, who did not deserve it and always looked to dharma.
ramayana-2-79-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-17.translation: Burning within, it tormented Raghava, as a hidden fire torments a tree scorched by a forest blaze.
ramayana-2-79-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-18.translation: Sweat born of the fire of grief poured from all his limbs, as the Himalaya, heated by the sun's rays, pours out its snow.
ramayana-2-79-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-19.translation: ...a mountain of sorrow whose caves were brooding, whose minerals were sighs, whose trees were misery, whose peaks were grief and exhaustion...
ramayana-2-79-19.meaning: His sorrow is pictured as a mountain.
ramayana-2-79-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-20.translation: ...whose beasts were confusion, whose herbs and bamboo were torment: Kaikeyi's son was overwhelmed by that great mountain of sorrow.
ramayana-2-79-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-79-21.translation: Then Guha, deeply troubled, comforted great-hearted Bharata, who had come with his people, about his elder brother.
ramayana-2-79-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 79: Guha, still wary of the huge army, asks Bharata whether he comes in friendship. Bharata assures him he is going only to bring Rama back. Guha praises him, but that night Bharata is crushed by grief for Rama.

ramayana-2-80-1.translation: Then Guha, who roamed the deep forest, told immeasurable Bharata about the noble devotion of great-souled Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-80-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-2.translation: To Lakshmana, who was awake, virtuous, holding a fine bow and arrows to guard his brother, I said:
ramayana-2-80-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-3.translation: 'Dear one, this comfortable bed has been prepared for you. Rest on it comfortably, joy of Raghava.'
ramayana-2-80-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-4.translation: 'All these people are used to hardship; you are used to comfort. Righteous one, we will keep watch to protect him.'
ramayana-2-80-4.meaning: Guha offered to keep watch instead.
ramayana-2-80-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-5.translation: 'There is no one on earth dearer to me than Rama. Do not be anxious; I tell you this truly before you.'
ramayana-2-80-5.meaning: Guha assures his love for Rama.
ramayana-2-80-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-6.translation: 'Through his grace I hope for great fame in this world, abundant merit and true wealth.'
ramayana-2-80-6.meaning: Rama's friendship is a blessing to him.
ramayana-2-80-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-7.translation: 'I will guard my dear friend Rama as he sleeps with Sita, bow in hand, together with all my kinsmen.'
ramayana-2-80-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-8.translation: 'There is nothing in this forest unknown to me, as I always roam here. We could withstand even a fourfold army in battle.'
ramayana-2-80-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-9.translation: When we said this, great-souled Lakshmana, looking only to dharma, answered all of us.
ramayana-2-80-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-10.translation: 'How, when Dasharatha's son lies on the ground with Sita, can I take sleep, or care about life or comforts?'
ramayana-2-80-10.meaning: Lakshmana cannot rest while Rama suffers.
ramayana-2-80-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-11.translation: 'Look, Guha, he whom all the gods and demons together cannot overcome in battle lies on grass with Sita.'
ramayana-2-80-11.meaning: He is pained at Rama's hardship.
ramayana-2-80-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-12.translation: 'Won by great austerity and many efforts, he is Dasharatha's only son with qualities like his own.'
ramayana-2-80-12.meaning: Rama was born after long prayer.
ramayana-2-80-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-13.translation: 'With him exiled, the king will not live long. Surely the earth will soon be widowed.'
ramayana-2-80-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-14.translation: 'The women, having cried out loudly, must have fallen silent from exhaustion. Surely the palace is silent today.'
ramayana-2-80-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-15.translation: 'Kausalya, the king and my mother: I do not expect that all of them will live through this night.'
ramayana-2-80-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-16.translation: 'My mother may live, looking to Shatrughna, but grieving Kausalya, mother of a hero, will perish.'
ramayana-2-80-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-17.translation: 'Without fulfilling his wish, which keeps passing him by, without placing Rama on the throne, my father will perish.'
ramayana-2-80-17.meaning: Dasharatha's hope will die with him.
ramayana-2-80-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-18.translation: 'Fortunate are those who, when that time comes, will perform all the funeral rites for the dead king.'
ramayana-2-80-18.meaning: He grieves he will not be at his father's rites.
ramayana-2-80-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-19.translation: '...the capital with lovely squares, well-laid-out main roads, mansions and palaces, adorned with every jewel...'
ramayana-2-80-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-20.translation: '...crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, ringing with music, full of every blessing, crowded with happy, well-fed people...'
ramayana-2-80-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-21.translation: '...full of parks and gardens, splendid with gatherings and festivals: happy people will walk about my father's capital.'
ramayana-2-80-21.meaning: Others will enjoy the city he has left.
ramayana-2-80-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-22.translation: 'May we, with the one true to his promise, return well when this period is over and enter it happily.'
ramayana-2-80-22.meaning: He hopes to return with Rama.
ramayana-2-80-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-23.translation: As the great-souled prince stood lamenting like this, that night passed.
ramayana-2-80-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-24.translation: At dawn, when the sun was clear, I had both of them, having matted their hair, ferried comfortably across on this bank of the Bhagirathi.
ramayana-2-80-24.meaning: Guha took them across the Ganga.
ramayana-2-80-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-80-25.translation: With matted hair and wearing bark clothes, mighty like leaders of elephant herds, carrying fine arrows, bows and swords, the scorchers of foes went, looking about them, with Sita.
ramayana-2-80-25.meaning: They went on into the forest.
ramayana-2-80-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 80: Guha tells Bharata how Lakshmana kept watch all night over Rama and Sita, refusing to sleep, grieving for his father and the queens, and how Guha ferried them across the Ganga the next morning.

ramayana-2-81-1.translation: Hearing Guha's very painful words, Bharata fell into deep thought right there where he heard them.
ramayana-2-81-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-2.translation: Delicate, of great strength, lion-shouldered, mighty-armed, with large lotus eyes, young and handsome...
ramayana-2-81-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-3.translation: ...after recovering for a moment, deeply dejected, he suddenly fell like an elephant pierced in the heart by goads.
ramayana-2-81-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-4.translation: Seeing Bharata in that state, Shatrughna, standing beside him, embraced him and wept aloud, senseless and wasted with grief.
ramayana-2-81-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-5.translation: Then all of Bharata's mothers rushed up, thin from fasting, miserable and wasted by grief for their husband.
ramayana-2-81-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-6.translation: Weeping, they surrounded him fallen on the ground, and Kausalya, sick at heart, went to him and embraced him.
ramayana-2-81-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-7.translation: As a loving cow embraces her calf, the ascetic queen, weeping and full of grief, embraced Bharata and questioned him.
ramayana-2-81-7.meaning: Kausalya treats him like her own child.
ramayana-2-81-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-8.translation: Son, I hope no illness afflicts your body? Today the life of this royal family depends on you.
ramayana-2-81-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-9.translation: Son, seeing you, I live. With Rama gone with his brother and King Dasharatha dead, you alone are our protector now.
ramayana-2-81-9.meaning: He is now her only support.
ramayana-2-81-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-10.translation: Son, I hope you have not heard anything bad about Lakshmana, or about my only son, gone to the forest with his wife?
ramayana-2-81-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-11.translation: Recovering for a moment, the famous one, still weeping, comforted Kausalya and said this to Guha.
ramayana-2-81-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-12.translation: Guha, tell me where my brother spent the night, where Sita and Lakshmana were, what bed he slept on and what he ate.
ramayana-2-81-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-13.translation: Asked thus, Guha, lord of the Nishadas, told Bharata how he had treated Rama, his dear and welcome guest.
ramayana-2-81-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-14.translation: I brought much food of every kind, delicacies and various fruits for Rama to eat.
ramayana-2-81-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-15.translation: Rama, true in valour, declined it all; remembering the duty of a Kshatriya, he did not accept it.
ramayana-2-81-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-16.translation: 'Friend, we must not accept; we must always give.' So, king, that great soul persuaded us.
ramayana-2-81-16.meaning: A ruler's role is to give, not to take.
ramayana-2-81-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-17.translation: The famous Raghava, with Sita, drank only the water Lakshmana brought and so kept a fast.
ramayana-2-81-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-18.translation: Then Lakshmana too drank the remaining water. The three, silent and composed, performed the evening prayer.
ramayana-2-81-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-19.translation: Then Sumitra's son quickly made a fine bed, bringing kusha grass himself for Raghava.
ramayana-2-81-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-20.translation: Rama lay on that bed with Sita, and Lakshmana, having washed their feet, stepped away.
ramayana-2-81-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-21.translation: This is the root of the ingudi tree, and this is the grass on which Rama and Sita both slept that night.
ramayana-2-81-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-22.translation: Fastening on his back two quivers full of arrows, with finger guards, and holding his great strung bow, Lakshmana, scorcher of foes, stood all night around him.
ramayana-2-81-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-81-23.translation: Then I too, holding a fine bow and arrows, stood where Lakshmana was, guarding the Indra-like one with my tireless kinsmen, bows in hand.
ramayana-2-81-23.meaning: Guha and his men kept watch too.
ramayana-2-81-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 81: Hearing of Rama's hardships, Bharata faints. The queens gather round him. Guha shows him where Rama slept and describes how Rama refused gifts and drank only water.

ramayana-2-82-1.translation: Hearing all this carefully with his ministers, Bharata went to the root of the ingudi tree and looked at Rama's bed.
