ramayana-2-90-12.translation: Told this by Rama, Lakshmana spoke, angry as a fire about to burn up that army.
ramayana-2-90-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-13.translation: Clearly Bharata, Kaikeyi's son, having been consecrated and wanting the kingdom secured, is coming to kill us both.
ramayana-2-90-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-14.translation: That great, splendid tree is clearly visible: the kovidara banner on the chariot, with its tall trunk, shines there.
ramayana-2-90-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-15.translation: They ride swift horses as they please; these riders shine, delighted, mounted on elephants.
ramayana-2-90-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-16.translation: Hero, let us take our bows and retreat to the mountain, or stay right here armed and ready. Perhaps the kovidara banner will come into our power in battle.
ramayana-2-90-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-17.translation: Perhaps I will see Bharata, because of whom you, Raghava, Sita and I have met with this great misfortune.
ramayana-2-90-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-18.translation: This enemy Bharata, because of whom you, Raghava, lost the eternal kingdom, has come, hero; he must be killed by me.
ramayana-2-90-18.meaning: Anger leads him to wrong conclusions.
ramayana-2-90-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-19.translation: I see no wrong in killing Bharata, Raghava. There is no sin in casting off one who has harmed us before. When he is dead, rule the whole earth.
ramayana-2-90-19.meaning: Lakshmana argues from anger, not wisdom.
ramayana-2-90-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-20.translation: Today let Kaikeyi, greedy for the kingdom, see her son killed by me in battle, deeply grieved, like a tree broken by an elephant.
ramayana-2-90-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-21.translation: I will kill Kaikeyi with her followers and kin. Let the earth be freed today from a great stain.
ramayana-2-90-21.meaning: His fury is extreme; Rama will correct him.
ramayana-2-90-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-22.translation: Today, giver of honour, I will release this restrained anger and insult on the enemy forces like fire on dry brush.
ramayana-2-90-22.meaning: He is ready to unleash his anger.
ramayana-2-90-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-23.translation: Today with sharp arrows, piercing enemy bodies, I will drench this forest of Chitrakuta with blood.
ramayana-2-90-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-24.translation: Let wild beasts drag away the elephants and horses whose hearts are pierced by my arrows, and the men I kill.
ramayana-2-90-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-90-25.translation: Having killed Bharata and his army in this great forest, I will without doubt be free of my debt to my arrows and bow.
ramayana-2-90-25.meaning: He feels his weapons demand action.
ramayana-2-90-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 90: Hearing the noise of a great army, Lakshmana climbs a tree and sees Bharata's banner. Assuming Bharata has come to kill them, he angrily vows to fight and kill Bharata and Kaikeyi. His outburst comes from loyalty and fear for Rama; in the next chapter Rama firmly corrects him.

ramayana-2-91-1.translation: Rama calmed Lakshmana, Sumitra's son, who was furious and overcome with anger, and said this.
ramayana-2-91-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-2.translation: What need is there here for a bow, or a sword and shield, when the great archer, the very wise Bharata, has come himself?
ramayana-2-91-2.meaning: There is nothing to fear from Bharata.
ramayana-2-91-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-3.translation: It is natural that Bharata wants to see us now. He would never even think of doing us harm.
ramayana-2-91-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-4.translation: When has Bharata ever done you any wrong? What fear is this that makes you suspect Bharata here today?
ramayana-2-91-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-5.translation: You must not speak harshly or unkindly of Bharata. If you wrong Bharata, it is I who am wronged.
ramayana-2-91-5.meaning: To hurt one's brother is to hurt oneself.
ramayana-2-91-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-6.translation: How could sons kill their father in any crisis, or a brother kill his brother, who is his own life, son of Sumitra?
ramayana-2-91-6.meaning: Family bonds should never turn to violence.
ramayana-2-91-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-7.translation: If you are saying this for the sake of the kingdom, when I see Bharata I will tell him, 'Give the kingdom to him.'
ramayana-2-91-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-8.translation: Lakshmana, if I tell Bharata truly, 'Give him the kingdom', he will say 'Certainly.'
ramayana-2-91-8.meaning: Rama is sure of Bharata's generosity.
ramayana-2-91-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-9.translation: Told this by his righteous brother, Lakshmana, devoted to his welfare, shrank into his own limbs with shame.
ramayana-2-91-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-10.translation: Seeing Lakshmana ashamed, Raghava replied: 'I think this mighty-armed one has come here to see us.'
ramayana-2-91-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-11.translation: Thinking of our forest life, he will take us home; or he may take Vaidehi, who is used to great comfort.
ramayana-2-91-11.meaning: Bharata may want to bring them back.
ramayana-2-91-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-12.translation: Those two fine horses of good breed shine there, hero, swift and as fast as the wind.
ramayana-2-91-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-13.translation: That huge elephant swaying at the front of the army is Shatrunjaya, the old elephant of our wise father.
ramayana-2-91-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.

ramayana-2-91-14.translation: Then Lakshmana, conqueror in battle, came down from the top of the sala tree and stood by Rama's side with folded hands.
ramayana-2-91-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 91: Rama calms Lakshmana. Bharata would never harm them, he says; brothers do not kill brothers. If Lakshmana wants the kingdom, Rama will ask Bharata to give it to him. Ashamed, Lakshmana falls silent.
